records.name: Conditional supplied lipid-membrane account
openObligations: Read the complete actual primary main article pages 153-165 and complete PMC HTML, all seven figures, all three tables, Methods/References, plus the complete six-page publisher Supporting Information with all four figures and procedures. The university PDF adds a repository cover. Primary supplement identity is verified by ACS figshare DOI 10.1021/acssynbio.7b00265.s001 and file 9445870; original PMC files were unread HTML challenges.

This reconstitution supplies purified mature enzymes and pre-existing phospholipid liposomes; enzymes and substrates are added externally. The source explicitly says this pathway does not support de novo membrane synthesis because PlsB and other components require existing phospholipids/membranes. No first membrane, protein biosynthesis origin, self-reproducing cell or self-made enzyme complement is established.

The selected chemistry context is the three-enzyme PA time course in SI Figure S3. It is distinct from the full eight-enzyme headgroup pathway and the PE/PG endpoint/calibration assays. SI specifies different PlsB/ATP concentrations for that time course than the general main PA procedure; these are retained as different preparations, not silently pooled.

LC-MS records internal-standard-normalized ion counts and source-assigned lipid identities. Species-dependent response, extraction recovery, peak integration and external calibration govern concentration/yield inference. The main text refers to PE/PG standards in Supporting Information, but the retrieved six-page supplement contains no explicit PE/PG calibration curve; no independent absolute-yield or uncertainty reconstruction is made.

Limiting-CoA conversion supports source-specific cofactor recycling, with supplied ATP and substrates. It does not close energy/resource supply, synthesize fatty-acid chains from carbon feedstock, make every phospholipid or show indefinite throughput. Small PA signal without PlsC is source-attributed to possible PlsC contamination of PlsB; omission effects are not treated as perfectly pure single-enzyme controls.

R18 self-quenching is a membrane dye-dilution proxy. In Figure 6 the immediate fluorescence increase follows oleic-acid addition and does not require phospholipid biosynthesis; subsequent PA conversion adds little further fluorescence change. Thus the signal alone cannot isolate synthesis-driven area growth from fatty-acid partition, swelling, fusion or dye redistribution.

The source reports an approximate 25-30 percent expansion from R18 assumptions. No new exact area/volume expansion, vesicle number, leaflet distribution, size distribution or calibrated membrane material balance is independently admitted. Triton-normalized maximal emission is not a direct bilayer surface-area standard.

R18 PA conversion uses 2.7 mM oleic acid and three enzymes. Figure 7 morphology follows a different PG-pathway preparation and a 1.5 mM total fatty-acid feed. These are not matched single-vesicle samples or an interchangeable protocol. Cryo-EM snapshots are not longitudinal lineage/continuous growth tracking.

High-dose material forms stacked multilamellar-like structures that resolve after EDTA. The dosed-feed comparison also lowers magnesium; exact lower magnesium concentration is not resolved in the reviewed main/SI descriptions. Feeding and magnesium are changed together, so an isolated feeding or magnesium causal effect is not established.

The PA-divalent-cation/outer-leaflet imbalance/slow-flip-flop explanation is a source hypothesis. No direct leaflet-resolved synthesis, flip-flop kinetics, cation binding map, complete membrane retention, permeability/selectivity panel, electrochemical gradient or transport activity is measured here.

The title continuous refers to CoA reuse and finite precursor conversion; the conclusion proposes a future continuously controlled feeding system. records.name: Prepared T4 lysozyme product-selection assay
openObligations: T4 WT* denotes the cysteine-free pseudo-wild-type scaffold; the compared proteins are prepared mutants, not all natural lysozymes. Activity in the halo assay is qualitative (+++,++, + or -), not a measured kcat or numerical fractional activity.

The 60-min T26H run uses 80 micromolar substrate and 0.5 micromolar enzyme at 0 C. Figure 2b,c use 2 micromolar substrate,5 min 25 C and different WT*/T26H enzyme concentrations (0.08 versus 0.5 micromolar), and are inherited from1995. No matched rate ratio is inferred across these runs.

The source estimated about 10:1 transglycosylation-to-hydrolysis products after60 min; this is a product ratio at that time and substrate concentration, not an initial-rate constant, kinetic selectivity coefficient or general efficiency ratio. No complete integration uncertainty is supplied.

Higher-mass peaks support longer glycan products, but PMC Table 2 peak numbering(6, 7 for trimer/tetramer) conflicts with main-text assignments (5, 6). Preserve this discrepancy rather than silently changing labels. The probable pentamer is tentative.

Mass assignment and product stereochemistry constrain a mechanism without directly observing a transient His26 covalent intermediate or transition state. A T26E adduct in this paper is inherited prior work; double-mutant adducts are only inferred from SDS/PAGE as explicitly noted.

The 60-min T26H chromatogram and inherited lower-concentration WT*/T26H comparisons do not provide a fully matched quantitative causal comparison of transglycosylation rates or independent replication.

openObligations: The16pairs are assayed separately with one monomer identity per reaction and a common helper; they do not measure simultaneous competition of all four monomers across all sequence contexts. The source explicitly leaves the stronger competition test open.

Figure3refers toFigure2conditions:200mM Tris pH8,100mM MgCl2,10/11micromolar primer/template and1mM AGC helper; its caption specifies50mM monomer whereas the associated Methods specify25mM. Preserve this unresolved source discrepancy rather than manufacture a single recipe or transfer its kobs to another concentration. Assay temperature is not uniquely stated in the selected captions/Methods.

The source reports triplicate-or-more experiments and SEM bars; the printed rate table contains central values and no full covariance. Rounded source values, the mean fidelity and confidence in each assay are not newly refitted or assigned a common uncertainty.

The source98% is a derived average of four separate rate-based fractions, rather than a directly sequenced error fraction or a universal per-base fidelity. The50nucleotide effective-genome discussion assumes an error-threshold model and is not a genome length observed to replicate or persist.

G:U wobble is a source-supported explanation for the faster mismatch, not a hydrogen-bond geometry measured by these gels. Binding affinity, melting free energy, structural selectivity, polarity and independent electrostatic contributions are not directly measured.

Mansy dC15/dA15/no-template controls show substrate/template dependence in a different modified-DNA system; they are not the16-pair fidelity experiment and cannot inherit this numerical discrimination.
